john.6.p1.b1.text: After this, Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee (that is, the Sea of Tiberias).

john.6.p1.b2.text: A large crowd followed Him because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick. Then Jesus went up on the mountain and sat down with His disciples.

john.6.p1.b3.text: Now the Jewish Feast of the Passover was near.

john.6.p2.b1.text: When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward Him, He said to Philip,

john.6.p2.b2.text: “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”

john.6.p2.b3.text: But He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do.

john.6.p2.b4.text: “Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece.”

john.6.p3.b1.text: One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him,

john.6.p3.b2.text: “Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?”

john.6.p3.b4.text: Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.

john.6.p4.b1.text: Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks,

john.6.p4.b2.text: and distributed to those who were seated

john.6.p5.b1.text: And when everyone was full, He said to His disciples,

john.6.p5.b2.text: “Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.”

john.6.p5.b3.text: So they collected them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.

john.6.p6.b1.text: “Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”

john.6.p6.b2.text: Then Jesus, realizing that they were about to come and make Him king by force, withdrew again to a mountain by Himself.

john.6.p7.b1.text: When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea,

john.6.p7.b2.text: It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet gone out to them.

john.6.p7.b3.text: A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew agitated.

john.6.p8.b1.text: they saw Jesus approaching the boat, walking on the sea—and they were terrified.

john.6.p8.b2.text: “It is I; do not be afraid.”

john.6.p8.b3.text: Then they were willing to take Him into the boat,

john.6.p8.b4.text: and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading.

john.6.p9.b1.text: The next day, … So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor His disciples were there,

john.6.p9.b2.text: they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.

john.6.p10.b1.text: it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.

john.6.p10.b2.text: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life,

john.6.p10.b3.text: “What must we do to perform the works of God?”

john.6.p10.b4.text: “The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.”

john.6.p11.b1.text: “What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You? What will You do?

john.6.p11.b2.text: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness,

john.6.p11.b3.text: it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.

john.6.p11.b4.text: For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”

john.6.p12.b1.text: “Sir,” … “give us this bread at all times.”

john.6.p12.b3.text: Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.

john.6.p12.b4.text: But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.

john.6.p13.b1.text: … the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.

john.6.p13.b2.text: For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.

john.6.p13.b3.text: … that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.

john.6.p13.b4.text: For it is My Father’s will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.”

john.6.p14.b1.text: “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?

john.6.p14.b2.text: How then can He say, ‘I have come down from heaven?’”

john.6.p14.b4.text: “No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him,

john.6.p15.b1.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, he who believes has eternal life.

john.6.p15.b2.text: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died.

john.6.p15.b3.text: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever.

john.6.p15.b4.text: And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh.”

john.6.p16.b1.text: “How can this man give us His flesh to eat?”

john.6.p16.b2.text: unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you.

john.6.p16.b3.text: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.

john.6.p16.b4.text: For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.

john.6.p17.b1.text: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.

john.6.p17.b2.text: This is the bread that came down from heaven. … the one who eats this bread will live forever.”

john.6.p17.b3.text: Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.

john.6.p18.b1.text: “This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?”

john.6.p18.b3.text: The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing.

john.6.p18.b4.text: The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.

john.6.p19.b1.text: However, there are some of you who do not believe.”

john.6.p19.b2.text: (For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.)

john.6.p19.b3.text: From that time on many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.

john.6.p20.b2.text: “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.

john.6.p20.b3.text: We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God.”

john.6.p21.b1.text: “Have I not chosen you, the Twelve?

john.6.p21.b2.text: Yet one of you is a devil!”

john.6.p21.b3.text: He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus.
